tutorial.title: Toggling CSS Classes
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to add, remove, or toggle classes with JavaScript

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
There's a reason why we haven't used setAttribute() to set classes. If we use it to change a class, it overrides the previous class.

We can see the issue if we run this code and try to make the player show as both hurt and powered up.

Make sure to pick setAttribute.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
There's a better way to add and remove classes and it's with a property called classList.

Press the buttons to try out different combinations and see it in action first.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
To add a new class without overriding the previous one, first, we have to add the classList property. Then, we can use it to access the add() method.

Make sure to pick . followed by classList and then ., add, (, ).

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
Inside the add() method, we code the class we want to add to the element.

Code "shield" to add the class once you call the function.

Make sure to pick ", followed by shield, and finally ".

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
Classes can be removed from an element as well. To remove a class, code the remove() method .

Make sure to pick remove.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we want to automatically add or remove a class when we call the function, we can use the toggle() method.

Run the code and press the button a few times to see it work.

Make sure to pick toggle.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can add multiple classes to an element at the same time. Let's add two new classes to our player.

Make sure to pick add("speedBoost", "doubleScore").

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can easily remove multiple classes as well. Remove the speedBoost and doubleScore classes from our player.

Make sure to pick "speedBoost", "doubleScore".

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the difference between using classList and setAttribute() to modify an element's classes?

setAttribute() overwrites the element's classes while classList does notclassList overwrites the element's classes while setAttribute() does not

setAttribute() overwrites the element's classes while classList does not.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which classList method would you use to add a class?

classList.add()classList.remove()

Make sure to pick classList.add().

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's happening in this code?

The hurt class is removed from the selected player elementThe player element is removed from the HTML document

The hurt class is removed from the selected player element.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we execute the togglePaused function if the selected element already has the paused class set?

The paused class is removed from the elementNothing happens; the element remains unchanged

The paused class is removed from the element.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when the addBuffs function is called?

The shield and speedBoost classes are added to the selected elementThe shield class is added to any element that has a speedBoost class

The shield and speedBoost classes are added to the selected element.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's wrong with this code?

Multiple classes should be separated by a commaYou can't remove multiple classes at the same time

Multiple classes should be separated by a comma.

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
To add the shield class to the selected element, code the classList property.

Make sure to type classList.

lessons.title: Lesson #16
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use the add() method to add the powered class to the player element.

Make sure to pick add followed by ( and then "powered", ).

lessons.title: Lesson #17
lessons.interactiveContent:
Remove the powered class from the selected element by coding the remove() method.

Make sure to type remove.

lessons.title: Lesson #18
lessons.interactiveContent:
Toggle the paused class by coding toggle("paused").

Make sure to type toggle("paused").

lessons.title: Lesson #19
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add two new classes to the selected element.

Make sure to pick "shield", "powered".

lessons.title: Lesson #20
lessons.interactiveContent:
Remove the hurt and powered classes.

Make sure to type "hurt",.
